strengths: Strong and consistent empirical results: 82% on RLBench (8% above HybridVLA), 72% on real-world Franka tasks, with 14× speedup over explicit CoT methods while improving performance
Comprehensive experimental evaluation spanning 10 simulation and 10 real-world tasks across three distinct embodiments (tabletop manipulation, mobile manipulation, dexterous hands)
Well-motivated approach clearly articulating limitations of explicit CoT methods (latency, representational bottlenecks, poor temporal consistency) and proposing a principled latent space solution

Thorough technical design: thoughtful multimodal latent representation (2D visual, 3D geometric, proprioceptive), elegant MoT architecture decoupling reasoning/action frequencies, and clever KV caching for efficient asynchronous execution

Excellent reproducibility and presentation: detailed architecture descriptions, systematic ablations isolating each component, comprehensive supplementary materials with hardware setups and failure case analysis
Practical impact: addresses real constraints in closed-loop robotic control by achieving 14× speedup without sacrificing performance
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primarily an engineering effort combining existing techniques (latent CoT from prior domains, MoT from Deng et al. 2025b, multimodal fusion, flow-matching). The adaptation to robotic manipulation is useful but incremental

Incomplete analysis of latent space: claims that latent CoT captures 'ineffable physical attributes' are asserted but not empirically validated. No probing experiments, mechanistic interpretability analysis, or validation that the model actually learns predicted future dynamics

Unresolved synthetic point cloud domain gap: pretraining uses synthetic point clouds from VGGT, but no real depth data is available at inference time. This significant domain gap is never ablated or analyzed, raising questions about whether the 3D geometric latent meaningfully contributes

Unjustified complex three-stage training recipe (freeze reasoning → train action → freeze action → train reasoning) with no ablation comparing to simpler joint end-to-end training or justification for this sequential approach

Real-world experiments limited to 200 demonstrations per task with no zero-shot, few-shot, or out-of-distribution evaluation. Long-horizon task (egg placement 3×) shows significant performance degradation (66%→47%→33%), suggesting unresolved challenges with error accumulation

Missing ablations and design choices: why 4-step temporal horizon (saturates at 4 but not explored beyond)? Why 1 token per modality (minimal gains shown beyond 1)? No comparison of cosine similarity loss to alternatives. No analysis of 3-stage training necessity

Scalability concerns: model is small (DeepSeek-LLM 1.5B). How does latent CoT scale to larger foundation models? Would larger models benefit differently from explicit vs. latent reasoning? These questions unaddressed

Limited comparison with world model baselines and recent future prediction methods. Inference speed breakdown not provided (how much time for reasoning vs. action?). Missing analysis of failure modes beyond 3 illustrative cases
